Mountmellick Town Team celebrated the launch of Mountmellick Town Centre 
First Plan on Tuesday 18th November 2025 in Mountmellick Library.  
The event was very well attended and welcomed by the wider community. The 
town team received funding for various groups in the town under the Healthy

The Regeneration Section have funded the Town Team to carry out a landscape 
enhancement project in the community garden in the village.   
The Town Regeneration Officer remains in discussions to acquire the old vacant 
national school on behalf of the Town Team to enable them to provide a 
community facility in the school. An application has been made to the 
Department to extend the deadline to conclude the transaction due to legacy 
paperwork issues.

November where the Town Team were presented with a preliminary design of 
the ‘The Square’ project in the town centre. This project includes a civic plaza for 
community events, a canopy and enhanced public realm.  
The Town Team advised they were happy for the project to proceed to Part 8. A 
public consultation is taking place on 16th December at which Council officials will 
be available to deal with queries on the project. The Town Team facilitated 
Healthy Ireland yoga and mindfulness classes in the town which will be completed

Walk and town center improvement works project.  The focus for the Town Team

Local Enterprise Office 
Overview of outputs delivered since the last monthly management report. 
• 
6 training courses were delivered to 78 participants including Start Your Own Business, 
bookkeeping and tax, and an information session for employers on the upcoming 
pension auto-enrolment changes which are coming into effect in January 2026.

2026 Training Courses 
Our spring 2026 training schedule will be published on the Laois website in the coming weeks. 
A broad range of programmes will be available to businesses and entrepreneurs including 
courses on financial management, artificial intelligence, social media, and management 
development programmes.  
 
Pension Auto-enrolment information sessions 
Pension Auto-enrolment is a new retirement savings system for employees that will be 
introduced on 1st January 2026. A webinar to understand what is changing, who it affects, and 
how to prepare was held on 4th December. This short session was aimed at employers who want 
practical guidance on their responsibilities. Another session will be taking place on 13th January 
to support employers to inform them on the new system which is coming into effect in 2026. 
 
Leadership and Management Development Programme 
LEO Laois recently invited expressions of interest for a planned a Leadership and Management 
Programme for business owners and key staff. A strong response was received and outlined the 
strong support for practical supports that strengthen strategic planning, people management and 
leadership capability. The programme will be delivered in early 2026, with final dates to be 
confirmed and published on the LEO website shortly for booking.

WP 3 Midlands ICT Action Plan  
 
Let’s TALK Sessions – Cybersecurity in Business (Longford) 
 
As 
part of 
the 
ongoing Let’s TALK regional engagement series, the Cybersecurity in Business event was 
successfully held in the Co:Worx Connected Hub in Longford, following the well-received 
session in Laois, Offaly and Westmeath. 
 
 
The event was well-attended and positively received, reinforcing the value of the Let’s 
TALK series as a platform for knowledge sharing, peer networking, and collaborative 
engagement within the tech and digital business community. These sessions continue to support 
businesses by signposting relevant services and supports, and by creating opportunities for 
collaboration and innovation across the region. 
 
 
Midlands ICT Network Site Visit – COMAND Gateway Centre 
 
On 27 November, the Midlands ICT Network organised a site visit to the COMAND Gateway 
Technology Centre at TUS for the ICT Network. These visits are an important part of our ICT 
Action Plan, giving businesses the chance to see first-hand the research, development, and 
innovation supports available in the region.

Robotics Competition Scrimmages

anticipation for the official Laois Regional Finals in January.

STEM in Schools and Communities 
The STEM Engagement Officer continued visits to schools, libraries and clubs for various STEM 
engagement activities including robotics workshops, rocket workshops, science and coding 
workshops. These workshops advance the skills of primary and secondary school students and 
promote similar subject retention in their education cycles. 
 
Science Week across Laois – Rocket Workshops 
The STEM Engagement Officer collaborated with branches of Laois Libraries and other venues 
to host a series of interactive Pop Rocket Workshops to primary school pupils. This workshop 
allows pupils to build a rocket from card and paper, decorate it, then learn about the physics of 
rocket science and aerodynamics

The day was filled with inspiration, creativity, and connection for people of all ages, leaving

Community Climate Action Fund: Community Garden Tour of Carlow  
As part of the Community Climate Action Fund, the Climate Action team organised a 
tour of community gardens in Co. Carlow for interested volunteer groups. The tour took 
place on 24th November and its purpose was to offer local volunteer groups a first-hand 
look at what well-directed climate and biodiversity funding can achieve. Four 
community gardens were visited on the tour. The volunteers at each garden showcased 
how even modest grants can transform unused or neglected spaces into productive, 
welcoming, and environmentally rich community hubs. Participants explored features 
such as pollinator-friendly planting, rainwater-harvesting systems, accessible raised 
beds, composting stations, and outdoor learning areas are all examples of practical, low-
carbon infrastructure that supports both people and nature. 
For the visiting Laois groups, the event was an opportunity to see how funding can 
amplify local energy, creativity, and community spirit. Seeing a fully established project 
in action can generate new ideas for their own towns and villages, from small-scale 
biodiversity improvements to larger collaborative climate initiatives.

A Raid in Clontyglass   
 
The Ballyfin Players took to Mountmellick Community Arts Centre on Friday November 
14 and 15 for two nights of amazing performances. 
 
'The Black and Tan Raid in Clontyglass', a commissioned work by Eileen Casey, is 
inspired by true events that took place in County Laois in 1921. 
Featuring local children alongside adult cast members, the group said that it brought 'a 
touching and authentic energy' to the story, as a 'powerful portrayal of life during 
turbulent times'. 
Co-producer with the Ballyfin Players, Mrs AC Reynolds, reflected on the community 
spirit found within the group. 
“There’s a great mix of comedy and drama this year. Having children on stage adds a 
lovely warmth, and it really shows what community theatre is all about," she said. 
This project was funded by Creative Ireland Laois’s Heritage through Art Grant scheme 
in 2023 and 2024. The project also received Decade of Centenary funding in 2025 
towards the recording of the play.
